text:
Maria G.: Heads-up — ticket #INC-2026-987 from a free-tier account (SparkApps) reporting spikes of 429s this morning. Customer says bursts happen when a scheduled job fires and then their client retries aggressively. They included a curl example and response headers.

Maria G.: Repro steps they gave:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' -d '{"model":"open-llama-7b","input":"batch job"}'
2) Run 30 of those in parallel from a CI job
3) Observe ~30% of requests return 429 with headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718800000
Retry-After: 60
```

Maria G.: They asked if we can temporarily raise caps or make an exception while they move to backoff + jitter. They also want to know upgrade path (free -> paid) and whether Sales can assist quickly.

support-bot: Created internal case INC-2026-987 and linked Zendesk ticket ZD-44121 :white_check_mark:

Alex R.: Thanks for the summary. A couple of quick Qs before approving any exception:
- Customer account id?
- Expected peak RPS and whether the parallel bursts are transient (cron) or sustained.
- Any PII in requests requiring private deployment?

Maria G.: Account id: acct_6789 (SparkApps). They said the bursts are transient (cron jobs every 6 hours lasting ~2 minutes). Peak concurrent requests reported ~40, average per-minute token rate ~25k tokens/min during the window. No PII, public app.

Jordan S.: I can take ownership of the upgrade conversation. If they're willing to move to paid (monthly commit) we can offer a reserved capacity trial and bump quota immediately via sales trial. What's the threshold we should push to avoid repeat incidents?

Lisa O.: Ops note: free-tier quota is soft-capped at 60 req/min and a small burst bucket of 120 for a short window. Paid tiers get higher base rates and a larger burst allowance. The 429s and headers look standard — Retry-After 60 means their token bucket emptied. Two parallel remediation paths:
- Short-term: grant a one-time burst window (48h) by updating their quota entry in the admin console, monitor and revert if we see abuse.
- Long-term: educate customer to add exponential backoff + jitter and/or move to a paid plan with higher sustained rates.

Lisa O.: Admin action to apply temporary burst (internal):
```
# web admin (internal): https://console.redwood.com/admin/accounts/acct_6789/quotas
# or CLI: redwood-admin quotas update --account acct_6789 --rate 180 --burst 400 --note "48h support exception"
```

Maria G.: Requested approval: one-time 48h burst increase to rate=180 req/min and burst=400. We'll patch their quota and message them that it's a short window while they implement backoff. We'll monitor logs and latency.

Alex R.: I don't love making permanent exceptions without Sales commitment. Approve a 24h temporary increase now; if Jordan gets a verbal commitment for upgrade within 7 days, extend to 48h. Post-condition: add monitoring alert to this case and document change in the support ticket.

Jordan S.: Understood — I'll reach out to SparkApps and offer an onboarding plan + 30-day paid trial for Dedicated/reserved. If they agree, we can convert their account and make quota permanent. I need a short blurb to send them about best practices to avoid 429s while they evaluate: can someone paste a succinct guidance?

Maria G.: Draft for customer message: 
"Hi SparkApps — we temporarily raised your request quota to reduce 429s while you migrate to a stable flow. Please implement exponential backoff with jitter and consider moving to a paid tier for sustained throughput. Example backoff (pseudo):
```
wait = base * (2 ** attempts) + random(0, jitter)
if wait > max_wait: abort/retry later
```
Also honor the Retry-After header from the API responses.     "

Lisa O.: Add the following practical client-side tuning for them:
- Limit parallel workers to <= 10 during migration
- Use token-level batching where possible to reduce per-request tokens
- If using scheduled jobs, add randomized start delay across runs to avoid spike alignment

Maria G.: I'll send that with the note that we applied a 24h increase per Alex's ok and we'll extend to 48h if Jordan secures upgrade commitment. Also will include this reproduction snippet and the headers so devs can correlate.

support-bot: Admin action pending: quota patch queued for acct_6789 by Maria G. (action id: act_9921)

Lisa O.: One more ops note — monitor the following logs for the next 12h:
- ingress.ratelimit.rejections for acct_6789
- gateway.latency.p95 for model open-llama-7b
If we see >5% 429s after the change, rollback and open an infra incident.

Alex R.: Approved. Maria, patch it and update ZD-44121 with the exact CLI command used and the monitoring playbook. Jordan please confirm once you have sales touch scheduled. Thanks. :thumbsup:

Maria G.: Patch applied (24h) and ZD-44121 updated with notes and the patch command. Messaging SparkApps now with the short guidance and the expected expiry time. I'll post here if they accept upgrade.

Jordan S.: Scheduled call with customer for 2026-04-01 10:00 PT. I'll report back.

Maria G.: Closing loop here. If anyone wants to review the customer message copy before I send, ping me.

support-bot: Case INC-2026-987 updated: quota_change=act_9921 status=applied by=Maria G.

Lisa O.: Thanks all — follow-up item: add a KB entry for free-tier burst exception flow and the exact admin CLI commands (ops playbook). I'll draft it and share in #eng-oncall.

Alex R.: Nice coordination. Leaving thread.

-- end of thread --
